$comment: Every third-party service the starter can use. All are optional: the product builds, runs and passes CI with none of them. Run `node scripts/setup.mjs` to see what is on and how to turn the rest on.

integrations.name: Sentry
integrations.purpose: Crash and error reports from the iOS, Android, web and back office apps
steps: Create an organisation, then one project per app: Apple iOS, Android, and React twice (web app, back office).
In each project open Settings → Client Keys (DSN) and copy the DSN.

integrations.name: Grafana Cloud
integrations.purpose: Backend traces, metrics and logs in SYST and Prod (Dev uses the local stack in observability/)
steps: Create a stack, then open Connections → OpenTelemetry (OTLP) and create a token.
Copy the OTLP endpoint and the Authorization header it shows.

integrations.name: Apple Developer Program
integrations.purpose: Running the iOS app on a phone, TestFlight, the App Store and push notifications
steps: Enrol, then note your Team ID (Membership details).
Register the bundle IDs from apps/ios/Config/*.xcconfig and an APNs key for push.
Set DEVELOPMENT_TEAM in Xcode (or project.yml) when you first run on a device.

integrations.name: Google Play Console and Firebase
integrations.purpose: Publishing the Android app and sending push notifications
integrations.cost: 25 USD once (Play); Firebase Cloud Messaging is free
steps: Create the app in Play Console with the application ID from apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts and enrol in Play App Signing.
For push, create a Firebase project, add the Android app and download google-services.json (keep it out of this public repository).

integrations.name: Backend and web hosting
integrations.purpose: Running the API, web app and back office for real customers
steps: Pick a host for the .NET API (Azure App Service, Fly.io, Render…) and one for the static web apps.
Point each app at the deployed API: apps/ios/Config/*.xcconfig, the Android FlavorConfig files and VITE_API_BASE_URL.
Add a deploy workflow that uses the GitHub Environment (Syst or Prod), so it receives the settings above.
